findings.issue: Mathlib's associatedPrimes is the radical variant (prime I with I = radical of Ann(x), see Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/AssociatedPrime/Basic.lean), not the classical Ann(x)=P that the Japanese text and answer use. Under the Noetherian hypothesis the two coincide (isAssociatedPrime_iff), so the card is true, but the answer proves the classical statement and never mentions the equivalence.

patch.answer_note: Add one sentence to the answer: for Noetherian R, a prime P is associated iff P=Ann(x) for some x (if P=rad Ann(x) then Ann(x) is primary, so Ass(Rx)={P}).

findings.issue: (1) Same radical-variant caveat for associatedPrimes as in associated_primes_finite; in the hard_negative, Ass(R) is empty only for the classical definition (with Mathlib's radical definition the nilradical (x_1,x_2,...) is associated to x_1), so the negative must say it uses the classical Ann(x). The prime is written '(x_i)' ambiguously. (2) OpenMath uses overloaded '*' for scalar action and a bare '0' for the zero of M with no carrier information.

hard_negative.statement: $x$が$R$の$A$における整閉包$C$上で代数的(非モニックな多項式の根)であれば、$x$は$R$上整である。
hard_negative.reason: モニックの仮定が必要である。$R=\mathbb{Z}$, $A=\mathbb{Q}$では$C=\mathbb{Z}$で、$x=1/2$は$2x-1=0$を満たす($\mathbb{Z}$係数の非モニック式の根)が、$\mathbb{Z}$上整でない。

patch.answer:
$R,A$を可換環、$A$を$R$代数、$C$を$R$上整な$A$の元全体とし、$x\in A$は$C$上整とする。
$x$は$C$係数のモニック多項式の根であり、その係数を$c_0,\dots,c_{n-1}$とする。各$c_i$は$R$上整である。$R_0=R$, $R_{k+1}=R_k[c_k]$($k=0,\dots,n-1$)とおく。$c_k$は$R$上整なので$R_k$上整であり、その整方程式の次数を$d_k$とすると、$R_{k+1}$は$1,c_k,\dots,c_k^{d_k-1}$で生成される$R_k$加群である。有限生成加群上の有限生成加群は、生成元どうしの積を生成元に取れば有限生成なので、$R'=R_n=R[c_0,\dots,c_{n-1}]$は有限生成$R$加群である。$x$は$R'$上整なので、$R'[x]$は$1,x,\dots,x^{n-1}$で生成される$R'$加群であり、したがって有限生成$R$加群である。
$R'[x]$は$1$を含む部分$R$代数なので、行列式の議論を使う。生成元$b_1,\dots,b_k$について$xb_i=\sum_ja_{ij}b_j$($a_{ij}\in R$の像)と書くと、$\det(xE-(a_{ij}))$がすべての$b_i$を消すので$0$である($1$は$b_i$の線形結合だから)。これは$x$についてのモニックな方程式なので、$x$は$R$上整である。

Lean target and text restrict M to the universe of Q (Module.Injective is universe-restricted); the classical fact holds for all M. OpenMath drops the universe condition and so states the stronger classical claim; the 'answer' is just the definition applied to g=id.

OpenMath quantifies the index i unguarded ((forall (i) (-> (< i m) ...))) so i ranges over all numbers below m, not 0..m-1 (Lean uses Fin m). The card proves only the existence half of the structure theorem; uniqueness of (n, p_i^{e_i}) is not claimed, and e_j may be 0.

Two parallel vocabularies for the same concepts: is_comm_ring/comm_ring, is_module/module_over, is_submodule/submodule_of, is_pid/principal_ideal_domain, zero_module (constant) vs zero_module_of (predicate); unify names so cross-domain retrieval matches.

Mathlib specifics matter: associatedPrimes is the radical variant, IsSemisimpleModule is ComplementedLattice, Module.Projective is 'summand of free on P', Module.Injective is universe-restricted, IsEquivalence = Full+Faithful+EssSurj; several cards are literally definitions or differ from the textbook notion unless the hypotheses (Noetherian) are used, and answers define the notion inconsistently (projective = lifting in cards 13 and 15, = summand of free in card 14).
Hard negatives are mostly sound counterexamples (I checked each); the weak ones lack a concrete witness (snake, adjunction_hom_bijection, limit_cone_unique, integral_over_integral_closure).
